goal: Every legally recognized wine geographical indication, appellation, denomination of origin, viticultural area and equivalent protected origin system globally, without a fame or size threshold.
policy: Never infer a legal GI from statistical planting geography.
Never omit a designation because it is commercially small or obscure.
Prefer the authority in the country of origin; treaty registers are reconciliation sources.
Store registration/effective dates and superseded legal versions when available.
A registry identity record does not imply that grapes, yields, ageing, styles or production rules are fully modeled.
Subzones, wards, districts, communes, climats, MGAs, crus and formally regulated named sites belong in the hierarchy when legally or officially defined.
Historical bottles must distinguish the designation/law actually in force at harvest from a modern geographic equivalent.

registries.notes: Product specifications and historical legal versions still require per-GI extraction.
AVA defines geography; it must not be treated as an EU-style grape/style prescription.

registries.system: Australian wine GIs and protected terms
registries.notes: 114 hierarchy records are indexed locally; Wine Australia's textual GI determinations remain legally controlling, and product/grape rules are separate.
Registered and enduring wine GI identities are indexed; individual legal/product detail remains a separate research layer.

registries.system: Japanese liquor geographical indications - wine subset

registries.notes: All 32 PDO wine identities announced by the National Wine Agency in April 2025 are indexed; product specifications are progressively extracted.
121 protected IG/DOC register rows from the September 2025 INV list are indexed, preserving same-name records by jurisdiction/legal class.

registries.system: Chilean viticultural zones / wine denominations of origin

registries.notes: Must ingest current geographical units, regions, districts and wards from current legal/certification records, not rely only on the older scheme booklet.

registries.system: Brazilian IP/DO geographical indications - wine subset

registries.notes: The same register also contains treaty-protected foreign wine names useful for reconciliation.

requiredRecordDepth: identity and protected spelling/transliteration
legal system and protection class
registration, effective, amendment and repeal dates
hierarchy and parent/child geography
official boundary definition and geometry when available
wine/product categories and colors/styles
authorized, principal and prohibited grapes
blend percentages and origin percentages
viticultural rules: density, training, pruning, irrigation, yield, harvest restrictions
minimum/maximum analytical parameters
winemaking practices required/permitted/prohibited
enrichment, acidification/deacidification, sweetening and fortification rules
pressing, extraction, fermentation and vessel requirements when specified
ageing and release rules by level/style
traditional terms and reserved label indications
old-vine/vine-age rules if any
named subzones, communes, crus, climats, MGAs, wards or vineyards when formal
soil, geology, topography and climate
historical vintage observations and authority assessments
historical legal version applicable to each vintage
